pairs.subject: background-jobs
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:63 Recurring background loops are spawned as unowned, detached tasks without registering through a central supervisor door, retaining no stop handle, and participating in no graceful shutdown drain.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/storage.rs:292 Recurring storage maintenance runs in an ad-hoc detached task without registering through a central supervisor door, retaining no stop handle, and lacking epochal shutdown draining.

crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:81 The recurring sweep execution lacks a panic capture barrier and a per-tick timeout deadline, causing any unhandled panic or hang to terminate or stall the background task silently.

crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:67 The sweep operates on a rigid fixed interval with no dual active/idle rates and no wake-on-signal hybrid to respond immediately when schedules are created or modified.

crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:117 The sweep emits log events only when work is found, emitting no per-tick health snapshots with closed-vocabulary outcomes and offering no independent silence detection.

crates/api/src/schedule_sweep.rs:69 Startup intentionally discards the immediate tick and lacks a bounded reconciliation sweep for orphaned jobs left in running or cancelling states by previous aborted processes.

crates/api/src/jobs.rs:127 The job queue implements cooperative two-step cancellation with in-flight jobs transitioned to cancelling until clean completion, alongside dedicated progress reporting and snapshot retrieval.
crates/api/src/jobs.rs:43 Job collection is implemented as an immediate snapshot read rather than a bounded wait handle over pending operations, so wait budget timeout semantics do not apply.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard primarily contemplates in-process supervised loops; when split across an API server and external workers, background work divides between local sweeps and durable job queues where distributed lease heartbeats replace in-process task supervisors.
